title: Getting Started
dek: What to expect in the beginning.

items.question: How do we begin?
items.answer: With a conversation. We’ll talk about your goals, your investments, and the questions keeping you up at night. If it feels like a good fit, we’ll map out a plan for moving forward.

items.question: What kind of clients do you work with?
items.answer: Mostly individuals and families who want thoughtful guidance around meaningful wealth. Many are entrepreneurs, professionals, or retirees who prefer a long-term partner rather than a transactional advisor.

items.question: Do you have a minimum to work with you?
items.answer: In most cases, clients have around $2M or more in investable assets. The number matters less than whether we can truly help you.

items.question: What happens in the first few meetings?
items.answer: We learn your full financial story—investments, taxes, estate planning, family priorities, and future goals. Then we build a plan that connects the pieces.

items.question: How long does it take to get everything set up?
items.answer: Usually a few weeks. Enough time to understand your situation and implement things carefully—never rushed.

items.question: Will moving my accounts to Fairview trigger a big tax bill?
items.answer: Not if we can help it. When you arrive with existing holdings, we unwind positions gradually and with tax impact in mind, rather than liquidating everything on day one.

items.question: Where are your offices?
items.answer: San Francisco Bay Area (Greenbrae, CA) and Pittsburgh, PA. We meet on your terms—phone, email, video, or in person. If it’s easier, we’ll come to you.

items.question: What exactly do you do for clients?
items.answer: We help people make good financial decisions over long periods of time. That includes planning, investment management, tax awareness, and ongoing advice.

items.question: How involved are you in managing investments?
items.answer: Very. Fairview does its own research and builds portfolios internally rather than outsourcing investment decisions.

more.label: How we research and build portfolios

items.question: Do you only manage investments?
items.answer: No. Investments are just one piece. We also help clients think through taxes, retirement, inheritance decisions, real estate, philanthropy, and other major financial choices.

items.question: Is financial planning included in the fee?
items.answer: Yes. Planning is part of the advisory fee—no separate planning charge. We start with your plan; the portfolio follows.

items.question: Do you advise on assets you don’t manage?
items.answer: Yes. Real estate, a concentrated business stake, an old 401(k), private holdings—if it affects your financial life, we include it in the overall plan at no extra charge.

more.label: How we think about your whole picture

items.question: Will I only work with one advisor?
items.answer: You’ll have a primary relationship, but you benefit from the entire Fairview team—advisors, analysts, and operations professionals working together.

items.question: What happens if my advisor leaves or retires?
items.answer: Your relationship isn’t tied to one person. Every account is known by more than one member of the team, and that continuity—across advisors, and across generations of your family—is part of how the firm is built.

items.question: Do you have a clean regulatory record?
items.answer: Yes. You can verify it yourself through FINRA BrokerCheck or the SEC’s Investment Adviser Public Disclosure site—we’d rather you check than take our word for it.

items.question: How often will we talk?
items.answer: Typically a few times a year, plus anytime something important comes up. Financial life rarely moves on a quarterly schedule.

title: Fees
dek: What you pay, in plain numbers.

items.question: What are your fees?
items.answer: One advisory fee based on assets we manage: 1.00% on assets up to $5 million, 0.75% above $5 million through $10 million, and 0.50% above $10 million. Updated March 2026.

items.question: What does the fee include?
items.answer: Financial planning, investment research, portfolio construction, ongoing guidance and reviews, and coordination across family accounts.

items.question: Do you charge commissions?
items.answer: No. No commissions, and no separate planning fees. One fee based on the assets we manage for you.

items.question: Do fees go down as assets grow?
items.answer: Yes. As assets increase, the percentage declines. We also combine assets across families, which can further reduce fees. Billed quarterly.

items.question: Who owns Fairview?
items.answer: The advisors who work here. The firm is 100% owned by the people who pick up when you call—not a bank, a board, or a private-equity buyer.

items.question: How much do you manage?
items.answer: About $2.14 billion under management, as of March 2026.

items.question: Do you hire salespeople or make cold calls?
items.answer: No. We’ve never hired a salesperson or made a cold call. The families at Fairview tend to arrive the same way: another client sent them.

items.question: Where is my money actually held?
items.answer: Your assets are held at independent custodians like Schwab or Fidelity. Fairview manages the investments but never holds the money itself.

items.question: Are you legally required to act in my best interest?
items.answer: Yes. As a Registered Investment Advisor, Fairview has a fiduciary duty to put clients’ interests first.

items.question: Can you move money without my approval?
items.answer: No. Any withdrawals or transfers require your authorization.

items.question: How do you handle client confidentiality?
items.answer: Even when we work with multiple generations of the same family, each relationship is treated as its own—information is never shared unless you ask us to.

items.question: How transparent is the investment process?
items.answer: Completely. You’ll know what you own, why you own it, how it’s performing, and what you’re paying.

items.question: How long do clients usually stay with Fairview?
items.answer: Many relationships last decades and often span multiple generations of a family.

items.question: What’s your basic investment philosophy?
items.answer: Own high-quality businesses and hold them for a long time. Markets move around in the short term, but strong companies tend to grow over time.

more.label: How we put that to work

items.question: Do you try to predict the market?
items.answer: No. We focus more on understanding businesses than predicting headlines.

items.question: Why do you use individual stocks instead of only funds?
items.answer: Owning a stock means owning part of a business. Fairview researches companies deeply and builds portfolios of carefully selected businesses expected to grow over time.

items.question: How diversified are your portfolios?
items.answer: We typically own a focused group of companies rather than hundreds of holdings—paired with other investments where appropriate.

items.question: What matters most for long-term investing?
items.answer: Patience. Staying invested through the ups and downs usually matters more than trying to be clever.

items.question: How do I track my portfolio and plan?
items.answer: Clients have access to a secure portal where they can see their investments, financial plan, and important documents anytime.

items.question: Can I see my entire financial life in one place?
items.answer: Yes. The planning platform can integrate outside accounts—banking, retirement plans, and brokerage accounts—so you can see everything together.

items.question: How does Fairview use technology in the investment process?
items.answer: Technology helps us analyze data, monitor portfolios, and stay organized. But investment decisions ultimately come from human judgment and experience.

items.question: Do you use artificial intelligence?
items.answer: Like many firms, we use modern analytical tools—including some AI—to help process information and improve efficiency. But decisions about your money are always made by people.

items.question: Will AI replace financial advisors?
items.answer: AI can analyze data. It can’t understand families, goals, or the emotions that come with money. Good advice still requires human judgment.

items.question: Is my financial information secure?
items.answer: Yes. The systems we use rely on encrypted connections, multi-factor authentication, and institutional custodians to protect your information.
